subject: Flowwise: rapid throughput degradation - recovery runbook and customer note
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@flowwise.io>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop impacting Flowwise production

Hi Lauren / Marissa —

We just saw a sharp drop in throughput across our production integration with Redwood starting ~08:55 PDT. Token throughput for the 256B model profile dropped ~65% and user-facing latency doubled (p95 from ~180ms to ~420ms). This is affecting our checkout pipeline and we've started to queue requests on our side.

Attached is a short screenshot of our internal telemetry (timeline-screenshot.png). We haven't changed traffic patterns on our end; this looks like something on the Redwood side. Can you confirm receipt and provide an ETA for workaround or mitigation? We're happy to be on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: sudden throughput drop impacting Flowwise production — triage + customer note

Lauren — quick triage update:
- Observed correlated KV-cache evictions and a spike in per-host allocator CPU around 08:50 PDT for the cluster serving Flowwise. The eviction rate jumped ~4x; cache miss amplification appears to be the primary driver of token latency.
- Mitigations applied (live):
  1) Reduced generation batch window for Flowwise tenant from 80ms -> 20ms (low-risk flip).
  2) Forced KV-cache warm for the last 5 hot prefixes for Flowwise (background warm job).
  3) Rolled routing rule to fall back to lp-quantized variant for 30% of Flowwise traffic to relieve kernel pressure.
- Immediate effect: token throughput recovered ~40% and p95 dropped from ~420ms to ~260ms in our internal metrics. Still not at baseline.

I'm attaching a short triage log (sre-triage-log.txt). Next: consider temporary reserved queue bump for the tenant and investigate why cache eviction correlated with allocator surge.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: sudden throughput drop impacting Flowwise production — triage + customer note

Adding engineering context and a short recovery runbook draft:
- Root cause hypothesis: a combination of bursty keyspace churn from a warm-up on Flowwise + allocator fragmentation on a subset of hosts. This created cascading KV-cache evictions that dramatically increased generation kernel work.
- Short-term product actions I can push in the next 30–90 minutes (low-risk):
  * Toggle per-tenant routing to send 25% of requests to a lower-memory, lp-quantized model variant (already started by SRE for 30% but we can expand to 50% if needed).
  * Reduce soft batching window globally for Flowwise to 10–20ms and tighten the tenant-level batching cap (implemented by SRE currently to 20ms).
  * Apply a temporary per-tenant cache budget increase for Flowwise (config flag) — requires infra approval (Ben), but this is reversible.
- Roadmap asks (post-incident):
  1) Telemetry: per-tenant KV-eviction metrics surfaced in Console (priority).
  2) Circuit-breaker: automatic per-tenant fallback when eviction rate > threshold.
  3) Warm-start helpers: tooling to pre-warm KV cache for big launches.

I've consolidated these steps into a quick runbook (flowwise-recovery-runbook.md) — please review. Happy to join the customer call; suggest we keep external comms focused on mitigation steps and ETA rather than internal root cause until we've verified.

— Soojin
Sooj in Lee
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@flowwise.io>, Flowwise Platform <platform@flowwise.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Flowwise service impact — mitigation applied and next steps (short customer note)

Hi Alex / Flowwise team —

Thanks for flagging this morning and apologies for the impact. Quick summary of what we've done and next steps:

What happened (short): Our runtime experienced a spike in KV-cache evictions in the cluster serving Flowwise that caused increased per-token work and a throughput degradation. We're continuing internal analysis; we will follow up with a fuller RCA once validated.

Mitigations completed (what we did right away):
- Reduced batching for Flowwise requests (80ms -> 20ms) and tightened batching caps.
- Forced KV-cache warm for hot prefixes and increased cache budget for Flowwise temporarily.
- Enabled partial routing to a lower-memory, lower-latency model variant to relieve host pressure.

Immediate customer impact: Throughput has improved ~40% from the peak regression and p95 latency has improved from ~420ms to ~260ms. We're still tracking to return to baseline and will keep you updated on progress.

Next steps and ETA:
- Short-term (0–2 hours): expand fallback routing to 50% if metrics do not return to baseline.
- Medium-term (today): complete reserved queue bump and full cache stabilization.
- Follow-up (48–72 hours): confirm root cause and schedule a postmortem + roadmap items (per-tenant eviction telemetry).

We know this impacts your checkout flow — we can offer a credit for the affected window once we finalize the incident sizing. If you'd like a quick bridge, we can join now; otherwise we'll send one consolidated status update in 1 hour.

Attached: customer-facing note draft (flowwise-cust-note-v1.docx) and our internal triage log.

Please let me know if you'd like us to expand the fallback immediately or join a call.

Apologies again and thanks for your patience —
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
